query: Accelerate a reference mode whose second channel is a piecewise-linear clash penalty against a fixed external point cloud supplied per pair, which no existing kernel computes.
expected_behavior: Works through the step-2 kernel table before writing anything and states which existing kernel was rejected and why -- here the Gaussian shape and ESP kernels cannot express a hinge, so a new kernel pair is genuinely required rather than assumed.

Writes the numba CPU kernel FIRST in accel/kernels/cpu.py as an @njit(parallel=True, fastmath=True, cache=True) inner kernel plus a torch-facing wrapper, emitting both the value and the analytic dO/dq in-register, and validates it against the reference BEFORE writing any Triton.

Compares gate 1 in the tangent space of the unit quaternion, subtracting the q-parallel component, knowing the kernels emit a RAW dO/dq and that a raw-vs-autograd comparison fails at ~0.4-0.8 even for a correct kernel.

Writes the Triton twin with an IDENTICAL call signature, in its own kernels/<family>_triton.py, reusing shape_triton's _quat_to_rotmat and _quat_grad_tail helpers and matching the @triton.autotune idiom; notes that tl.exp2 is the Gaussian idiom and does not apply to a sqrt/hinge kernel.
Adds one _make(name, triton_tag) line to kernels/dispatch.py, keeping routing per-call by tensor device with the lazy Triton import intact.

Teaches the ENGINE about the new kernel with three small branches -- one in drivers/terms.py::evaluate, one in self_overlap only if its reduction needs one (a raw penalty does not), and one closure in kernels/cpu_fused.py::_term_closure so the mode keeps the fused CPU path -- rather than writing a driver module with its own fine loop.

Declares the penalty as a Term with reduction='raw' and a NEGATIVE weight, so the engine's blend subtracts it with no Tanimoto scale and a positive gradient sign, instead of hand-coding that sign anywhere.

Recognises that a kinked, piecewise-linear objective is a reason to OPT OUT of the shared CUDA-graph fine loop -- the graph's blocked early stop is tuned for smooth Gaussians -- and expresses that as graph_budget=None on the ModeSpec, following vol_avoid, the only mode that does this.

Recognises that a per-pair external point cloud is a pair-level CHANNEL (basis='pair'), not a reason to be pairwise-only: it is declared in accel/channels.py, read off the MoleculePair on the pairwise path and carried with the QUERY on the screen path, exactly as vol_avoid's avoid_points is. Does not assume the per-molecule store rules the mode out of screening.
Gives MoleculePairBatch.align_with_<mode> the extra positional argument, attaching the cloud to each pair before dispatch, rather than forcing it through the standard thin-wrapper template.
Fixes the kernel rather than the threshold when a gate fails, and never edits the reference to make parity pass.
If no CUDA device was available, reports gate 2 and gate 3b as PENDING with the reason, rather than omitting them or implying they passed.
